newsitem.title: USA: Safeco, St. Paul Cos. report higher second quarter.
newsitem.headline: Safeco, St. Paul Cos. report higher second quarter.

text.p: Safeco Corp., reporting higher second-quarter earnings, said Monday its results were aided by fewer weather-related catastrophes and narrowed losses in its homeowners insurance business.
The Seattle-based insurer posted net income of $117 million, or 93 cents a share, compared with $106.0 million, or 84 cents a share, the year before.
A First Call consensus estimate of 20 analysts had put the company's earnings at 80 cents a share for the second quarter.
Revenues rose to $1.08 billion from $1.02 billion a year earlier.

The company's property and casualty operations posted a $24 million underwriting profit, compared with $4.4 million last year. Safeco attributed the improvement primarily to its homeowners line narrowing its underwriting loss to $4.4 million in the quarter, compared with a $19 million loss last year.

Safeco said that good results in its personal auto, surety and commercial insurance businesses contributed to its property and casualty quarterly pretax income of $93 million, compared with a $74 million profit last year.

The company's life and health operations reported a $35.7 million quarterly pretax profit, compared with $37.3 million last year. Safeco's real estate, credit and asset management operations reported quarterly profits of $2.8 million, $5.3 million and $1.4 million, respectively.
The St. Paul Cos., based in Saint Paul, Minn., also reported higher second-quarter results.
The group of companies provides property-liability insurance and reinsurance underwriting throughout the world.

"Our underwriting results continue to be quite acceptable, despite the significant flood-related losses we incurred in Minnesota and North Dakota in the second quarter," Chairman Douglas W. Leatherdale said.
For the quarter, earnings rose to $230.5 million, or $2.50 a share, compared with $130.0 million, or $1.42 a share, a year earlier.
Revenues rose to $1.62 billion from $1.36 billion a year ago.
St. Paul Cos. stock was up 81.25 cents at $82.3125 on the New York Stock Exchange and Safeco was up 68.75 cents at $46.50 on Nasdaq.
